key_insight: SpiderCSS turns ideal CSS state specifications into provably fault-tolerant, CNOT-minimal preparation circuits using ZX-calculus rewrites and a modular compilation pipeline.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable way to reduce depth and qubit overhead for logical-state preparation, which is a key bottleneck in practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: Start from an ideal CSS-state ZX diagram.
Apply only fault-equivalent rewrites to preserve fault tolerance.
Compile the resulting diagram into a modular, CNOT-minimal state-preparation circuit.
evidence_signal: Monte Carlo results across CSS codes up to distance 15 show improved scalability, reduced depth and qubit footprint, a 33.7% average drop in logical error rate, and a 9.5% higher acceptance rate versus existing methods.
watch_item: The approach is specialized to CSS codes and relies on diagrammatic compilation quality, so performance may depend on code structure and implementation details.
paper_title: SpiderCSS: Scalable Fault-Tolerant CSS State Preparation
